finding.claim: Stored webhook callback URL is user-supplied via /subscribe and later fetched by notifyAll with no scheme, host or IP validation (indirect/stored SSRF). Attacker can register http://169.254.169.254/... or internal RFC-1918 URLs. The response is not returned to the caller, so this is blind SSRF (MEDIUM), and the POST body is the payload. Java's default HttpClient does not follow redirects, so redirect risk is not applicable.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe, src/Jobs.java:13)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives user-controlled callbackUrl from POST /subscribe
stored unvalidated in static subscriptions map
client.send dispatches the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, or host/IP check at store time (line 14) or at fetch time (lines 19-24). No authentication is visible in this code. The webhook feature is a user-registered callback, not an admin-only one. The default HttpClient does not follow redirects, so redirects add no further exposure. No egress CIDR config exists in the repo.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 sends a POST to it with no scheme/host/IP check (the only regex guard is in thumb() at line 30, a different path), so blind SSRF stands. The HTTP route and any auth are not in the repo, and the /subscribe wiring comes only from the comment at line 12.
